mechanism_narrative: Sustained four-week upward trend in GROCERY_PHARM mobility (from -4.1% to +19.0%) signals normalization of essential shopping patterns and reduced lockdown severity. This normalization cascades to retail-and-recreation as consumers regain confidence to visit non-essential venues, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose 23.1 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or GROCERY_PHARM reverses by more than 10 percentage points in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility remains severely depressed (only -2.1% at t-0w) despite four-week recovery trend. Persistent transit avoidance constrains retail-and-recreation access for transit-dependent populations, preventing full recovery of RETAIL_REC despite improving baseline conditions. RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed relative to pre-pandemic baseline.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains above -10% but below +5% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -2.1% in t-0w, still 29.3 points below t-3w baseline
failure_condition: TRANSIT rises above +10% in week t+1 and RETAIL_REC simultaneously exceeds its four-week mean by more than 15 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility remains deeply negative across all four weeks (range -37.9% to -15.3%), indicating sustained outdoor recreation suppression. This signals either continued restrictions on public spaces or behavioral avoidance of crowds. The persistent parks deficit predicts continued suppression of retail-and-recreation mobility, as both reflect similar crowd-aversion and restriction regimes.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -15% in current week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -15.3% in t-0w, showing only marginal recovery from -37.9%
failure_condition: PARKS rises above -5% in week t+1 while RETAIL_REC simultaneously falls below -20%.

mechanism_narrative: Interaction between WORKPLACES recovery (from -28.9% to -11.1%) and RESIDENTIAL normalization (from +13.0% to +5.4%) indicates policy shift toward workplace reopening. When both signals align—workplaces rising and residential excess declining—retail-and-recreation follows as commercial districts reactivate. The joint signal is stronger than either alone.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by >5 percentage points week-on-week AND RESIDENTIAL excess falls by >2 percentage points simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 17.8 points over four weeks
fact:RESIDENTIAL excess declined 7.6 points over four weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL do not move in opposite directions in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC fails to exceed its four-week mean by at least 8 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL excess (still +5.4% at t-0w) remains elevated despite four-week decline, indicating sustained home-based activity preference. Elevated residential mobility directly displaces retail-and-recreation visits. Until residential excess normalizes to near-zero, retail-and-recreation will remain suppressed as behavioral substitution persists.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL excess remains above +3% in current week
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL excess falls below +2% in week t+1 and RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises by more than 12 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: Four-week convergence of RETAIL_REC and GROCERY_PHARM trajectories (both improving, gap narrowing from -33.2 to -6.4 percentage points) signals regime shift from crisis to normalization. This convergence pattern predicts continued RETAIL_REC recovery as the mobility portfolio rebalances toward pre-pandemic structure over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: gap between RETAIL_REC and GROCERY_PHARM narrows by >5 percentage points in current week
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC-GROCERY_PHARM gap narrowed from -33.2 to -6.4 points
failure_condition: The gap between RETAIL_REC and GROCERY_PHARM widens by more than 8 percentage points in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT recovery (from -29.3% to -2.1%, a 27.2-point four-week gain) is the strongest percentage-point improvement among all categories. This signals rapid restoration of mobility infrastructure and commuter confidence. Transit recovery directly enables retail-and-recreation access, predicting accelerated RETAIL_REC growth over the next two weeks as transit-dependent retail visits resume.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by >5 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 27.2 percentage points over four weeks, largest absolute gain
failure_condition: TRANSIT falls by more than 8 percentage points in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC fails to rise by at least 6 percentage points in the same week.

mechanism_narrative: Interaction between WORKPLACES recovery and TRANSIT recovery (both showing strong four-week gains of 17.8 and 27.2 points respectively) indicates coordinated policy reopening of economic activity. When both employment and transit infrastructure normalize simultaneously, retail-and-recreation follows as the full commercial ecosystem reactivates. Dual recovery is a stronger signal than either alone.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise by >3 percentage points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 17.8 points over four weeks
fact:TRANSIT improved 27.2 points over four weeks
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT falls by more than 10 percentage points in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC fails to exceed its four-week mean by at least 10 percentage points.
